78-Inputs can arrive in any order.

82-- The mapper keeps the latest client KEXINIT payload it sent,

85-- When a KEX_ECDH_REPLY (31) arrives,
86-  and the mapper has both KEXINIT payloads and a private key,
87-  it computes the shared secret, the exchange hash H and the session id
88-  (H of the first exchange, never replaced on rekey),
89-  and derives *pending* keys (RFC 4253 section 7.2).
90-  If it is missing something, it derives nothing.
91-- Pending keys are kept **per direction** and are consumed when installed:
92-  each key exchange that completes (a KEX_ECDH_REPLY processed as above) gives one pending key set for outgoing
93-  and one for incoming.
94-- Sending `NEWKEYS` switches the **outgoing** direction to its pending keys, if there are any, and clears them;
95-  otherwise the outgoing direction keeps its current keys, cipher state and sequence number unchanged.
96-- Receiving NEWKEYS from the server switches the **incoming** direction to its pending keys, if there are any, and clears them;
97-  otherwise the incoming direction is unchanged.
98-  (Re-installing already used keys would restart the AES-CTR keystream, and the peer would see a MAC failure that is
99-  an artifact of the mapper, not behaviour of the server.)
100-- Strict KEX applies when the mapper offered it and the server's **first** KEXINIT of the connection contained `kex-strict-s-v00@openssh.com`.

102-  (OpenSSH PROTOCOL §1.9; Go x/crypto/ssh and libssh omit it when rekeying but keep resetting sequence numbers).
103-  Then the outgoing sequence number resets to 0 when sending NEWKEYS installs new keys,
104-  and the incoming one resets to 0 when receiving NEWKEYS installs new keys.
105-- Sequence numbers count every packet in each direction from the start of the connection (uint32, wrapping).
106-- The channel inputs `CH_CLOSE`, `CH_EOF`, `CH_DATA` and `CH_REQUEST_EXEC` use the server's channel id

108-  If no channel is open, the mapper sends nothing and the output is `NO_CHANNEL`.
109-  `CH_OPEN` is always sent.
110-  After the mapper sends or receives CHANNEL_CLOSE, the channel is no longer open.
111-- The mapper never answers server messages on its own:

# Paramiko 5.1.0: blocked by native KEX support

Pinned to the latest stable PyPI release checked on 2026-11-07:
https://pypi.org/project/paramiko/5.1.0/

The threaded ServerInterface server uses native transport defaults, a generated
RSA host key, password-only test/test authentication, session channels and exec
completion with status 0. No algorithms are patched or aliased.

Validation:

```sh
SMLEARN_TARGETS=paramiko uv run pytest -q tests/test_ssh_mapper.py
```

The initial invocation hit a sandbox restriction writing Docker buildx activity
under ~/.docker. Re-running with BUILDX_CONFIG=/tmp/paramiko-buildx succeeded in
building and running the tests: **5 failed, 11 passed, 1 skipped**.
Full assertion output is in validation.txt; server output is in negotiation.txt.

| Test | Result |
| --- | --- |
| alphabet_is_complete | PASS |
| happy_path_completes | FAIL |
| strict_kex_is_negotiated | PASS |
| wrong_password_fails | FAIL |
| session_works_after_auth | FAIL |
| no_channel_sends_nothing | PASS |
| disconnect_then_no_conn | PASS |
| trace_records_packets | FAIL |
| queries_are_deterministic, seq0 through seq6 | PASS (each) |
| newkeys_without_new_kex_keeps_keys | SKIP (OpenSSH-only) |
| rekey_after_auth_installs_fresh_keys | FAIL |

The first client KEXINIT produces CLOSED. Server output:

```text
paramiko.ssh_exception.IncompatiblePeer: Incompatible ssh peer (no acceptable kex algorithm)
```

Upstream source reference: the PyPI 5.1.0 source distribution, paramiko/transport.py
lines 215–226 (_preferred_kex), line 335 (_kex_info), and lines 2429–2444
(_parse_kex_init). Its sole Curve25519 name is
`curve25519-sha256@libssh.org`; it does not implement the mapper's required
`curve25519-sha256` name. The parser raises IncompatiblePeer when there is no
intersection. Source archive:
https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/76/cb/b1fde76618d84b1acf54d3d03d2b833ba5878afd12b9899346cc080f209d/paramiko-5.1.0.tar.gz

Strict KEX is supported and its negotiation test passes. Authentication, channel,
exec, and rekey behavior cannot be validated with this mapper because initial
key exchange fails. Determinism passes cover the resulting closed connections.
Stopped without a workaround, as required for implementation differences.
# golang-xcrypto

Pinned implementation: `golang.org/x/crypto v0.58.0`, the latest stable release
reported by the Go module proxy on 2026-11-07. Exact tag commit:
`8fdf07b3114278fb3b78c1cf1814e08bd851eb4c`.
Registry metadata: https://proxy.golang.org/golang.org/x/crypto/@v/v0.58.0.info

## Rekey compatibility finding

The complete failing query returns:

```text
KEXINIT -> NO_RESP
KEX30 -> KEX31+NEWKEYS
NEWKEYS -> NO_RESP
SR_AUTH -> SERVICE_ACCEPT
UA_PW_OK -> UA_SUCCESS
KEXINIT -> KEXINIT
KEX30 -> KEX31+NEWKEYS
NEWKEYS -> NO_RESP
CH_OPEN -> CLOSED
```

x/crypto advertises `kex-strict-s-v00@openssh.com` only in the initial
KEXINIT (`ssh/handshake.go`, lines 542–544), sets strict mode during the
initial exchange (lines 683–688), and retains that mode for subsequent
exchanges. Its transport resets sequence numbers on NEWKEYS whenever
strict mode is active (`ssh/transport.go`, lines 149–155 and 199–206).

Exact upstream sources:

- https://go.googlesource.com/crypto/+/refs/tags/v0.58.0/ssh/handshake.go
- https://go.googlesource.com/crypto/+/refs/tags/v0.58.0/ssh/transport.go

The mapper recomputes `strict_kex_active` on every received KEXINIT
(`src/smlearn/ssh/mapper.py`, line 85). The rekey KEXINIT lacks the marker,
so the mapper stops resetting its sequence numbers while Go continues to
reset them. This explains the closure on the next channel-open packet.
No algorithm mismatch was observed. Per the onboarding rules, no workaround
or mapper modification was made; successful rekey validation remains blocked
by this compatibility difference.

## Authenticated rekey difference

A separate reproduction using the unchanged mapper and testbed produced:

```text
initial strict_kex_active: True
KEXINIT => NO_RESP strict= True
KEX30 => KEX31+NEWKEYS strict= True
NEWKEYS => NO_RESP strict= True
SR_AUTH => SERVICE_ACCEPT strict= True
UA_PW_OK => UA_SUCCESS strict= True
KEXINIT => KEXINIT strict= False
KEX30 => KEX31+NEWKEYS strict= False
NEWKEYS => NO_RESP strict= False
CH_OPEN => NO_RESP strict= False
```

The initial server KEXINIT includes `kex-strict-s-v00@openssh.com`;
the authenticated rekey KEXINIT omits it. Both offer curve25519-sha256.
The mapper sets strict_kex_active to False on receipt of the second KEXINIT.
libssh retains strict KEX and resets packet sequence numbers on NEWKEYS.
This gives incompatible sequence numbers for the following encrypted traffic.
The test fails at the final CH_OPEN_SUCCESS assertion (actual: NO_RESP),
after both key exchanges have returned KEX31+NEWKEYS.

Relevant libssh source references, all in the exact official
[0.12.2 source archive](https://www.libssh.org/files/0.12/libssh-0.12.2.tar.xz):

- `src/server.c:226–231`, ssh_server_set_kex: explicitly skips appending
  extensions during authenticated rekey.
- `src/kex.c:916–945`, ssh_kex_append_extensions: appends the server strict
  KEX marker to the initial algorithm list.
- `src/kex.c:557–565`: enables the persistent SSH_SESSION_FLAG_KEX_STRICT
  when the client offers strict KEX.
- `src/packet.c:2100–2102`: resets send_seq on NEWKEYS in strict KEX.
- `src/packet_cb.c:164–166`: resets recv_seq on NEWKEYS in strict KEX.

The unchanged mapper's SSHMapper._received assigns strict_kex_active from
whether each received KEXINIT contains the server marker, and _install uses
that value to decide whether to reset sequence numbers. The mismatch is
therefore an interoperability finding, not a missing cipher or a target
configuration error. No workaround was applied; work stopped as requested.
All-pass validation could not be achieved under the rule prohibiting mapper
changes and workarounds for implementation behavior differences.
